emails.job: Get a prospective buyer to assess Resend as the SMTP provider for Supabase Auth before their next public launch or increase in signup volume.

emails.objection: Will connecting another sender actually resolve the limit on Auth email?
must_not_say: Do not say Resend SMTP or a Supabase plan upgrade automatically removes Supabase’s Auth rate limit.
Do not imply Resend’s Free plan has no daily cap.
Do not claim Resend detects or prevents Supabase Auth Hook changes that clear SMTP settings.
Do not claim Resend explains how Supabase counts requests against its hourly limit.
Leave out Broadcasts, dedicated IPs, security certifications, customer logos, and the full SDK list.
Do not describe Resend’s existing SMTP capability as newly released.
Do not state or imply that every reader uses Supabase. Present this integration conditionally (for example, 'If you use Supabase...') unless the user-supplied campaign context establishes it.

emails.why_it_fails: Upgrading Supabase’s plan does not raise the built-in email provider’s limit. A custom SMTP provider and a separate Auth rate-limit adjustment are required.
emails.mechanism: Resend provides Supabase-specific SMTP setup instructions and a destination for SMTP credentials. After connecting SMTP, the engineer must adjust Supabase’s initial 30-message-per-hour Auth limit as appropriate. Resend’s Free plan allows 100 emails per day.

emails.next_step_value: See Resend’s Supabase-specific SMTP setup instructions and where to obtain the credentials.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the guide does not change Supabase’s Auth limit, select a Resend plan, or validate production sending.

events.subject: Send Supabase Auth email through Resend
events.preview_text: See the SMTP setup and the separate sending limits to check.
events.body:
If you use Supabase Auth, you can send signup and login emails through Resend.

Resend is an email sending platform for developers, available as an SMTP provider for Supabase Auth. Our setup guide shows where to enable SMTP in Supabase and where to find your Resend credentials.

Before a public launch or an increase in signups, check the limits as well as the connection. Adding a sender alone does not change Supabase’s Auth rate limit.

With custom SMTP, Supabase initially limits Auth sending to **30 messages per hour**. You can adjust that separately in Auth Rate Limits. Resend’s Free plan also has a **100-email daily cap**.

Read the Supabase SMTP guide.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Two email limits to check before launch"
events.subject: Two email limits to check before launch
events.preview_text: Compare provider sending terms with Supabase’s separate Auth rate limit.
events.body:
If you use Supabase Auth, custom SMTP lets you route signup and login emails through a provider you choose. Supabase still applies its own Auth rate limit, which you adjust separately.

Resend is available as an email sending platform for transactional messages over SMTP. Pro includes **50,000 emails per month with no daily email limit**. Additional emails on Pro are billed at $0.90 per 1,000.

The Free plan has a **100-email daily limit**. Once custom SMTP is configured, Supabase initially limits Auth email to 30 messages per hour; that setting can be adjusted under Authentication > Rate Limits.

Before a public launch or an increase in signups, compare the provider’s sending terms with your expected volume, then check Supabase’s separate Auth setting. View pricing to compare Resend’s plan limits and overage terms.
